messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: private cluster 'acme-corp-prod' GPU request queue latency > 10s (gpu_queue_delay). autoscaler reported 0/3 successful node boots. Paging on-call: @dave and eng-runtime: @ben.


dave: ack, taking it. switching to incident channel. can someone drop the rollout link and the affected customer?

carla: customer = acme-corp, reported increased errors and slow inference at 11:02 PDT. support ticket #ACME-733 opened. they say most requests are queued for 10-20s then timeout.

ben: seeing the same in metrics — queue length spiked ~11:00 after a burst. autoscaler triggered, but node pool shows instances stuck in PROVISIONING -> BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT. 3 attempts in last 12m.

jessica: quick check: quota available in customer's VPC? cloud quota looks fine. no obvious throttling on cloud provider side.

mike: posting relevant logs from the cluster control plane:
```
E0312 11:04:03 node_boot: instance i-0a12e failed to run cloud-init: exit status 1
WARN 11:04:03 kubelet: failed to register node: TLS handshake timeout
INFO 11:05:10 autoscaler: launch attempt 2 -> i-0b34f, status=BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT
```

ben: digging into the bootstrap logs from one of the hosts (we have syslog snippets from the provider):
```
cloud-init[123]: Running user-data scripts
cloud-init[123]: error: failed to fetch package list: timeout connecting to mirror
systemd[1]: runc.service: Start request repeated too quickly
-- Reboot --
cloud-init[123]: final message: cloud-init v.19 finished with errors
```

dave: hmm. cloud-init failures + TLS errors. Could be private network routing in customer VPC preventing nodes from reaching our bootstrap endpoints (or mirror). Any recent customer firewall/route changes?

carla: customer says they rolled a VPC endpoint change yesterday to tighten egress.

ben: that fits. autoscaler keeps trying but new nodes can't complete bootstrapping because outbound egress to our artifact host and package mirrors is blocked. autoscaler hits scale limit (we've configured backoff after 3 failed boots). queue keeps growing.

ops-bot: Derived impact: ~40% request failure rate for acme-corp's private deployment; 95th latency degraded from 120ms -> 8.3s. Incident severity: P1 (customer-facing SLA degradation).

dave: immediate mitigation options:
- temporarily route traffic for acme-corp to hosted fallback model (requires customer opt-in)
- request customer to open egress for our bootstrap endpoints / mirrors
- manually pre-provision warm nodes using an alternate subnet with looser egress and attach to their pool (requires org access)

mike: on the warm nodes idea — we can try launching instances in an adjacent subnet their infra team controls. but that needs IAM and customer's sign-off.

carla: pinging customer contact now with proposed options; will ask for permission to open a temporary exception for our bootstrap hosts and to allow us to provision in their adjacent subnet.

jessica: meanwhile, can we increase the autoscaler retry limit to force more attempts? Might be pointless if bootstrap fails due to networking. Also risk of wasting instance quota.

ben: agreed — no point until networking is fixed. let's avoid hitting cloud API quotas. Focus comms and fallbacks.

carla: customer replied: "we can open egress to artifacts.redwood.internal and to apt mirrors for 30 minutes. prepping firewall rule now." They also asked for ETA.

dave: great. once rule is in, we need to trigger a manual re-provision for the stuck instances and scale the pool by +4 to catch up queued requests. ben, can you coordinate the reprovision steps?

ben: yes. plan:
1) pause autoscaler (so it doesn't oscillate)
2) delete the 3 stuck pending nodes to allow fresh launches
3) manually scale nodepool desired=+4 (create nodes in same launch template)
4) monitor kubelet registration and runtime readiness

I'll run commands and post progress.

ben: pausing autoscaler now.

ben: deleting stuck nodes (ids: i-0a12e, i-0b34f, i-0c56d).

ben: scaling nodepool +4 -> desired=8 (was 4). launching.

mike: firewall rule just applied by customer (carla updated). they allowed egress to artifacts.redwood.internal and to primary apt mirror.

ben: good sign — new instances starting, cloud-init output now shows package fetch success.

ben: kubelet registration: node-12 online, node-13 online. container runtime ready. attaching to pool.

ops-bot: autoscaler events: successful boots 2/4. Remaining 2 still initializing. queue length dropping 35% in last 6m.

carla: customer reports some immediate improvement in request latency. still seeing intermittent 5-6s tails.

dave: continue to monitor. keep autoscaler paused until we confirm stable. Also open a follow-up action to propose a warm pool strategy and recommend customers add explicit egress to our bootstrap endpoints in their hardened VPC runbooks.

ben: agreed. I'll create a runbook patch and a short script to pre-warm nodes via the customer's approved subnet.

mike: note for post-incident: autoscaler gave up after N failures due to default backoff; consider adding a distinct flow for private clusters that pauses the backoff if customer-specified egress exception is present (so operator can rapidly re-try after network fix).

dave: good product/ops item. We'll triage in eng-runtime backlog.

carla: customer support message being sent: "We've provisioned additional nodes and traffic should be improving. We recommend keeping the temporary egress rule for 30min to ensure warm nodes fully bootstrap. We'll follow up with a post-incident summary and recommended runbook changes."

jessica: adding incident labels: root cause = customer VPC egress restrictions preventing node bootstrap; contributing = autoscaler retry/backoff policy + lack of warm pool; impact = request queuing and timeouts; mitigation = temporary egress rule + manual reprovision and scaling.

dave: handoff to oncall monitoring: keep watch on acme-corp cluster for 2 hours, then we close this channel and start postmortem. If queue rises > 50% of current baseline, re-open.

ben: creating follow-up task ENG-RUNTIME-789 to add warm-pool recommendations and autoscaler config flag for private clusters.

mike: customer says: "thanks, we'll revert the rule in 45 mins."

carla: marking ticket #ACME-733 as monitoring, awaiting postmortem.

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Queue length for acme-corp down to +12% over baseline; error rate trending down. Severity downgraded to P2.

dave: thanks everyone. documenting timeline for postmortem. I'll take lead on RCA and include recommended changes: improve telemetry for bootstrap failures, make warm pool easy to enable for private clusters, and update customer-facing docs about required egress for node provisioning.

carla: I'll draft the customer-facing incident summary and send to acme contact for approval.

ben: closing out my immediate tasks; leaving logs and commands used in the incident runbook appendix.

ops-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (provisional): status=monitoring, next action: postmortem in 48h.
